question.problem:
Given  the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,4t⟩$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=⟨\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$
{{field-1}}$,0\,⟩$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{4}{5}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{-\frac{3}{5}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩}{(\frac{3}{5})}=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$
